title: Introduce ephemeral priority-limbo window and transparent restore orchestrator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: During multiple regional congestion episodes we observed thrashing where tenants toggled between soft-quarantine and active routing, causing spikey latency and cascading evictions. Motivation: Introduce a short-lived, transparent "priority-limbo" window that holds requests for tenants recently transitioned out of a degraded state and orchestrate a phased restore to prevent immediate oscillation. This PR implements a lightweight orchestrator that:
- Marks affected tenants into a limbo state for a configurable window (default 10s).
- Applies conservative admission (reduced concurrency) and gradual weight ramp during limbo.
- Emits limbo lifecycle telemetry and an auditable restore trace for postmortems.
- Exposes tuning knobs via config and runtime feature flags for canary rollout.
Design highlights:
- Limbo is per-tenant and shard-aware; the orchestrator keeps a small in-memory slot map (bounded) and relies on durable lease events from the controlplane to avoid split-brain.
- Restore policy: incremental unfreeze with N-step concurrency ramp (default 3 steps), backoff on observed SLO regressions.
- Safety: global cap on simultaneous limbo slots per node and a fast-bail path (force-evict) when memory or kv-pressure crosses thresholds.
- Observability: new metrics (limbo_slots, limbo_transition_latency, limbo_restore_failures), structured audit logs for each transition, and a dashboard template included.
Checklist:
- [x] Core orchestrator and limbo state machine
- [x] Admission and phased ramp logic
- [x] Telemetry & audit logs + Grafana dashboard template
- [x] Unit tests for state transitions and safety gates
- [x] Integration smoke test against simulated congestion harness
- [x] Feature flag gate and rollout playbook

Commits summary: single squash containing the orchestrator implementation (pkg/orchestrator/limbo_*), controlplane hooks (controlplane/events.go), admission adapter (runtime/admission/limbo_adapter.go), telemetry + dashboard (telemetry/limbo_metrics.go + dashboards/limbo.json), and tests (tests/limbo_state_test.go + integration/limbo_integration.sh). Rationale for squash: prefer single-commit rollout for easier backouts and bisecting in incidents.

review_comments: Diego Ramirez: Nice approach. Two quick asks: (1) add a unit test that simulates repeated rapid transitions to ensure we don't leak limbo slots, and (2) make the default limbo window configurable via env override with a sane upper bound.

Maya Chen: Added slot-leak unit test and env override in internal/config; also added a guard that caps the effective limbo window to 60s to address the upper bound concern. See tests/limbo_state_test.go commit.
Anya Singh: Can we avoid a global in-memory cap blowup if the controlplane emits a storm of events? Suggest rate-limiting event processing and an exponential backoff per-tenant.
Maya Chen: Implemented rate-limited event consumer and per-tenant exponential backoff; added metrics for dropped events. Updated integration test to simulate event storm.
Evelyn Park: Telemetry looks good. Please ensure dashboard panels include both limbo_restore_failures and per-step latency so SRE can quickly triage.
Maya Chen: Dashboard updated and sample alerts added in docs/ops/limbo_playbook.md. Ready for merge when CI is green.
CI Bot: initial unit test run failed (race detected in limbo_manager).
Maya Chen: Fixed race by swapping to a sync.Map for slot registry and added a concurrency test. Reran CI.
Diego Ramirez: LGTM pending one small comment about log verbosity.
Maya Chen: Reduced debug logs on every transition and left an audit-level log with structured fields.
merge_details: Merged by Evelyn Park via squash-merge. PR was rolled out behind a feature flag and gradually enabled in Canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over two hours. No rollback needed.
release_notes: Introduced an ephemeral 'priority-limbo' orchestrator to stabilize tenant restores after transient degradations. Adds new telemetry (limbo_slots, limbo_transition_latency, limbo_restore_failures) and an operational playbook. Default limbo window is 10s (configurable, max 60s).
post_merge_actions: Monitor limbo_restore_failures and limbo_transition_latency dashboards for 24h after full rollout
Run retrospective to evaluate default ramp steps (ENG-1678) and consider adaptive step sizing
Coordinate with support to update incident runbooks (docs/ops/limbo_playbook.md)
